title: [1/6/2023] Number of people per household in the UK in 1981 and 2001
prompt: The chart below compares the number of people per household in the UK in 1981 and 2001. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart presents information on the percentage of individuals in the UK residing in households of various sizes in the years 1981 and 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was a shift towards smaller households in the UK over this 20-year period, with an increase in the proportions of 1- and 2-person households, while the other groups showed a downward trend. Moreover, in both years, the most common living arrangement comprised of 2 individuals.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with smaller households, in 1981, single-person households accounted for 17%, only half of those with 2 residents, at 31%. This highest proportion was followed by 3-person and 4-person households, with figures of 20% and 18% respectively, while the percentages for those with 5 and 6 occupants were significantly lower, standing at 8% and 6% in that order.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: After 20 years, the figure for the household size of 2 members increased slightly by 3%, much lower than the growth rate of single-person households, surging by 9% and surpassing 3- and 4-person households. These latter two categories saw decreases of 3% each, to 17% and 15% respectively. Larger households, specifically those with 5 and 6 individuals, also experienced a decline, falling to 6% and 2% respectively by the end of the period.
